cards.text: Through Haggai the prophet, the LORD told Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, Joshua, the high priest, and the people that His house lies in ruins while each of them is busy with his own house. That word came on the first day of the sixth month, and the LORD said He had summoned a drought. I bet everybody's standing there like me when the smoke alarm goes off and I KNOW it's my batch.

cards.question: Zerubbabel, Joshua and all the remnant of the people have heard the LORD's message through Haggai. What do they do with it?

answers.text: They obey the voice of the LORD
They return to their own houses
They wait until the time has come

cards.question: The leaders and the people obey the words of the prophet Haggai, because the LORD their God had ___ him.

cards.text: So the people feared the LORD. Then Haggai, the messenger of the LORD, brings them another message, and this one is SHORT. Friend, I've cracked open fortune cookies with longer fortunes.

cards.question: Haggai brings a short new message from the LORD to the people who just obeyed. What does the LORD say?

cards.text: Then something happens inside Zerubbabel, the governor. His spirit gets stirred up, like dough that finally starts to rise after you've been staring at it for an hour.

cards.question: Somebody stirs the spirit of Zerubbabel, the governor. Who is it?
Only the two leaders get their spirits stirred by the LORD, and the rest of the people just follow along.

cards.text: And with their spirits stirred, they don't schedule a meeting to plan the next meeting. They COME.

cards.question: Their spirits stirred, the people come and begin the work on the ___ of the LORD of Hosts, their God.

cards.text: The text even gives the start date: the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of the king. I spent YEARS in a drawer waiting for somebody to get around to me, so trust me, I notice a date.

cards.question: The work on the house of the LORD begins in the second year of a king. Which king is it?

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: one about the people fearing the LORD, one introducing Haggai's short message, and one for the fortune-cookie joke. Non-opening story cards are limited to two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
